pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which comes first in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. mat
   B. market
   C. mother
   D. mango

2. Which noun needs the article 'the' because there is only one? (1 mark)
   A. chair
   B. boy
   C. sun
   D. mango

3. Articles: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya is beautiful.
   B. The Kenya is beautiful.
   C. An Kenya is beautiful.
   D. A Kenya is beautiful.

4. An invitation is (1 mark)
   A. a gift
   B. a big meal
   C. a card or message that asks a person to come to an event
   D. a song

5. What is the plural of 'monkey'? (1 mark)
   A. monkeys
   B. monkeis
   C. monkies
   D. monkeyes

6. 'The sun was as warm as a fresh loaf of bread.' This sentence uses (1 mark)
   A. a command
   B. a question
   C. a simile
   D. a list

7. When do we say 'I beg your pardon'? (1 mark)
   A. When we say goodbye
   B. When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   C. When we are hungry
   D. When we win

8. Which letter is silent in 'knife'? (1 mark)
   A. f
   B. k
   C. n
   D. e

9. First aid words: Which word has the sound /ɒ/? (1 mark)
   A. doctor
   B. bite
   C. pain
   D. snake

10. Which word goes before a noun to show ownership? (1 mark)
   A. mine
   B. my
   C. hers
   D. yours

11. Listening and diet: Which word has the sound /æ/? (1 mark)
   A. fruit
   B. food
   C. apple
   D. juice

12. Which noun is uncountable? (1 mark)
   A. chair
   B. pupil
   C. milk
   D. egg

13. 'There are ___ books on the desk.' Which fits a positive statement? (1 mark)
   A. much
   B. some
   C. any
   D. how

14. Which online reading habit is safe? (1 mark)
   A. Giving your address to a website
   B. Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   C. Visiting any page a stranger suggests
   D. Clicking every advert

15. How should the initials of Peter Otieno Juma be written? (1 mark)
   A. p, o, Juma
   B. P. O. Juma
   C. P O Juma,
   D. p.o.juma

16. What does it mean to read in phrases? (1 mark)
   A. To read backwards
   B. To read one letter at a time
   C. To read groups of words that go together
   D. To read only the first word of each line

17. What is a virus? (1 mark)
   A. A sharp tool
   B. A tiny germ that can make people ill
   C. A type of food
   D. A kind of medicine

18. Which word is an adverb of place? (1 mark)
   A. gently
   B. outside
   C. always
   D. soon

19. Which word has the long vowel /iː/? (1 mark)
   A. sheep
   B. ship
   C. sit
   D. bit

20. What is hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
   B. A school subject only
   C. Playing with friends
   D. A type of exercise

21. According to the text, when should we wash our hands? (1 mark)
   A. Never with soap
   B. After using the toilet
   C. Only on Sundays
   D. Only when we see dirt

22. What is a topic sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A list of adjectives
   B. A question at the end
   C. The last word of the paragraph
   D. A sentence that tells what the paragraph is about

23. How long is a descriptive composition at this level? (1 mark)
   A. 500 words
   B. 10 to 20 words
   C. 200 to 300 words
   D. 80 to 100 words

24. Who is a coach? (1 mark)
   A. The person who sells kit
   B. A person who trains a team
   C. The team's fans
   D. The person who blows the whistle

25. In netball, what must a player do with the ball after catching it? (1 mark)
   A. Sit on it
   B. Kick it
   C. Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   D. Run with it

26. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A long story
   B. A page of a dictionary
   C. A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   D. A kind of song

27. Which word ends with the sound /ŋ/? (1 mark)
   A. sin
   B. sun
   C. sum
   D. sing

28. How do newspapers and magazines usually differ? (1 mark)
   A. They are the same
   B. Newspapers have no words
   C. Magazines have no pictures
   D. Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures

29. Which page of a magazine lists the articles and their page numbers? (1 mark)
   A. The comic page
   B. The contents page
   C. The cover
   D. The advert page

30. Which preposition shows movement from one side to the other inside something, such as a gate? (1 mark)
   A. through
   B. under
   C. over
   D. near

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write about 60 words about these pictures: (1) A boy plants a seed. (2) He waters it every day. (3) A tall plant grows. (5 marks)

32. Write three sentences you would say to report an accident to an adult. (3 marks)

33. Write three sentences using three of these words: because, different, address, favourite, tomorrow. (3 marks)

34. List three things you can do to remember what you have read. (3 marks)

35. Describe how to find facts about a lion in a junior encyclopaedia. (4 marks)

36. Choose the correct word in each: (a) I (know / no) the answer. (b) They put (their / there) bags (their / there). (3 marks)

37. Write a title and an opening sentence for a story about a girl who finds a lost phone. (2 marks)

38. Explain three uses of the comma with an example for each. (5 marks)

39. Explain the difference between a factual and an inferential question and give an example of each from the story. (4 marks)

40. Correct the sentences: (a) 'Him is a driver.' (b) 'Give the pen to she.' (c) 'The bag is mine bag.' (3 marks)

41. Explain what the saying 'A stitch in time saves nine' teaches. (2 marks)

42. Name the three parts of a narrative and say what goes in each. (3 marks)

43. Correct the paragraph: 'last friday our class visited the museum. mr. juma told us about kenya.' (4 marks)

44. Write two sentences using a simile of your own about a celebration. (4 marks)

45. Write an introduction of two sentences for the topic 'A day I enjoyed'. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — mango
   Mango has n as the third letter, which comes before r, t and the o in mother.

2. C — sun
   There is only one sun, so we say the sun.

3. A — Kenya is beautiful.
   We do not use the before most country names.

4. C — a card or message that asks a person to come to an event
   An invitation invites someone to an event.

5. A — monkeys
   A vowel comes before y, so just add s.

6. C — a simile
   It compares the sun to bread using as ... as.

7. B — When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
   It asks a person to repeat or says sorry.

8. B — k
   We say nife, so the k is silent.

9. A — doctor
   Doctor has the short vowel /ɒ/.

10. B — my
   My comes before a noun. Mine stands alone.

11. C — apple
   Apple has /æ/.

12. C — milk
   We cannot count milk one by one.

13. B — some
   Some is used in positive statements.

14. B — Reading only pages approved by a teacher or parent
   Approved pages keep you safe online.

15. B — P. O. Juma
   Capital initials each followed by a full stop.

16. C — To read groups of words that go together
   Chunking words into phrases makes reading smoother.

17. B — A tiny germ that can make people ill
   A virus is a tiny germ.

18. B — outside
   'Outside' tells where.

19. A — sheep
   'Sheep' has a long /iː/; the others have a short /ɪ/.

20. A — Keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
   Hygiene protects us from germs.

21. B — After using the toilet
   The text lists after using the toilet, before eating and more.

22. D — A sentence that tells what the paragraph is about
   It states the main idea.

23. D — 80 to 100 words
   The task calls for 80 to 100 words.

24. B — A person who trains a team
   A coach trains players.

25. C — Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   The passage says players cannot run with the ball.

26. C — A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   Proverbs teach lessons.

27. D — sing
   'Sing' ends with /ŋ/.

28. D — Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   Newspapers are published often and carry news.

29. B — The contents page
   The contents page shows where to find each article.

30. A — through
   'Through' shows movement within.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: One morning, Musa planted a seed in the garden. Every day he watered it. After some weeks, a small green shoot appeared. At last, a tall plant grew and Musa was proud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, order, linking words, past tense, punctuation and length.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Help! There is an emergency. A boy has fallen and his arm is bleeding. Please bring the first aid kit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear sentence.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences using the words with correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write new words and meanings; say one sentence about each chapter; draw a story map; retell the story to a partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct suggestion.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the topic Lion, find the L volume or type it in the search box, use guide words or the index to find the page, read the text, pictures and captions and write short notes in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) know (b) their, there
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct choice.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title: An Honest Girl. One morning, Achieng found a phone near the school gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: In lists: rice, beans and cabbage. After yes or no: Yes, I can. When addressing a person: Mama, come here. Also before but/so between sentences.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use and example (max 5 including quality of examples).

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has its answer stated in the text: 'Where was Omondi's mother?' An inferential question needs clues: 'How did Omondi feel at the start?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for each example.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) He is a driver. (b) Give the pen to her. (c) The bag is mine. / It is my bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It teaches us to fix a small problem early, before it becomes a big problem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 mark for avoiding a bigger problem.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events and problem. End: how it is solved and how people felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Last Friday our class visited the museum. Mr. Juma told us about Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Last Friday, Mr. Juma, Kenya and correct full stops.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The cake was as sweet as honey. The children danced like leaves in the wind.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence with a correct simile.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: It was a sunny Sunday in Kisumu. My family went to the lake for a picnic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for when or where and 1 mark for who or what.
